content.text:
Recommended challenge verdict: FAIL for all five plans and the program. All five spec hashes match, and every acceptance criterion is listed in at least one task. The blockers are execution ordering, missing implementation ownership, and verification that cannot prove the claimed behavior.

1. Critical — Orchestration duplicates shared authority and depends on convergence that it also proposes to implement.

   `SPEC-RELEASE-ORCHESTRATION-003/T001` adds `ReleaseObservationEvidence`, `ReleaseReceipt`, artifact contracts, and prepared bindings; these already belong to product `PM-001/PM-002` and convergence `T1/T3`. Orchestration `T002` repeats product identity, fixture exclusion, slot derivation, and DAG construction. Its `T003` waits for the entire convergence implementation to pass, then adds the provider adapters and receipt emission that convergence must already have to pass. It also still names `ArtifactManifestV1` after product requires replacing that shape.

   These tasks collide in `callisto-model/src/release.rs` and graph `release.rs`, `release_artifacts.rs`, and `release_execution.rs`. The architecture model explicitly keeps prepared effect authority graph-private and makes `.github` a consumer.

   Correction: make product the sole owner of product/slot derivation, convergence the sole owner of observation/dispatch/receipts, and orchestration the consumer of completed contracts. Reduce orchestration T001–T004 to genuinely orchestration-specific handoffs, historical-run validation, and CLI exposure. Record qualified cross-plan prerequisites in an executable program ordering.

2. Critical — Exact registry publication bytes have no concrete implementation task.

   Product `PM-005` validates artifacts; convergence `T3` observes external bytes and `T4` changes execution order. None specifies replacing the actual packaging/submission seam or proving outgoing bytes before submission. Orchestration `T003` vaguely adds adapters only after convergence is supposed to pass.

   Live evidence: graph `release.rs:370` calls `cargo_publish_argv`, `npm_publish_argv`, and a PyPI build/upload pair. `registry_argv.rs:63` publishes a Cargo manifest; `:196` publishes npm workspaces through npm/pnpm/Yarn/Bun; `:284` rebuilds Python distributions and uploads a glob. Those APIs accept neither validated artifact bytes nor an expected digest.

   Therefore a validated manifest can coexist with publication of newly generated, different bytes. Post-publication observation detects the mistake after an irreversible effect. This leaves product AC-006 and convergence AC-006/013 incomplete.

   Correction: assign convergence an explicit dispatch migration covering Cargo, every npm manager path, and individual PyPI distribution files. Name the helper files and eliminate workspace packaging authority after validation. Test captured outgoing bytes and pre-submission rejection of regenerated mismatches, plus partial PyPI uploads.

3. High — Product and membership batches cannot satisfy their own compilation gates.

   Product `PM-001/PM-002` remove old wire types and package-owned operation fields while downstream callers migrate only in `PM-004/PM-005` and convergence. Yet the first batch runs workspace tests/lints. Existing graph `release_execution.rs:10,40,71,190` imports and constructs `ArtifactManifestV1`/`ArtifactSlotId`; graph `release.rs:395` reads `id.package`. Removing those contracts first breaks these consumers.

   Membership `M-001` changes Cargo/uv readers and the shared glob builder to return `Result`, but `IgnoreWalkLocator` migration is deferred to M-002/M-003. Its existing callers at `locate/ignore_walk.rs:38–40` still consume direct membership values. Existing npm membership construction also calls the same glob builder (`membership.rs:359,364`). M-B1 contains only M-001 but requires `just test` to pass.

   Correction: make breaking signatures and all immediate consumers one compilation transaction. Split nonbreaking preparation separately if useful; do not retain compatibility decoders. Product’s no-orphan dispatch gate also needs task-level ordering with convergence rather than making the entire product plan a prerequisite for code needed to satisfy its gate.

4. High — Required distribution verification is only name-checked.

   Product AC-005 requires macOS ad-hoc signing and local verification, both Linux architecture/static-link checks and native execution, and the real release-profile WASM payload in Moon/Extism. `PM-005` claims this criterion but tests manifest validation. Orchestration `T005/T007` say “native and WASM smoke tests” without assigning codesign/static-link checks or changing the sandbox’s artifact input.

   Live evidence: `crates/callisto-moon/tests/moon_wasm_sandbox.rs:41` loads `target/wasm32-wasip1/debug/callisto_moon.wasm` and stages a debug fixture at `:90`. Existing `just wasm-check` also builds without `--release`. Passing these gates cannot establish that the shipped WASM file works.

   Correction: assign concrete build validation commands and matching native runners, extend the sandbox to consume the exact release artifact, and bind verification to the final payload digest. Include deliberately wrong architecture, dynamic linkage, unsigned/invalid macOS, and broken release-WASM negatives.

5. High — Fixture classification has no configured representation or complete implementation boundary.

   Product `PM-003` proposes recording a dev-only classification in `callisto.toml`, but only owns that file and `release_decision.rs`. Live `config/raw.rs:5,71,94` denies unknown fields; package configuration exposes `release-trigger`, `publish-to`, etc., with no dev-only release classification. Resolved configuration also has no proposed field.

   The task does not choose whether an existing setting supplies this meaning or add the new raw/resolved field and propagation. Adding an invented key fails configuration loading; merely removing the fixture from a fixed group fails the promised coordinated source-version behavior.

   Correction: specify the exact representation, own raw/resolved configuration and its propagation, and test exclusion from decision authority while preserving source version updates. Prove both explicit selection rejection and that fixtures cannot appear through dependency/prerequisite derivation.

6. High — Setup does not close the existing WASM cache-hit bypass.

   Setup `S-001–S-004` centralize resolution and verification but never assign cache identity/revalidation behavior. Live `setup-callisto-wasm/action.yml:27` keys the cache by unresolved `inputs.version`, and `:31` skips the download step on a cache hit. A literal `latest` cache can remain indefinitely old; replacing only inline download logic with the helper leaves cache hits outside resolution and verification.

   Correction: resolve the immutable identity before lookup and always validate cached bytes/provenance, or remove this cache. Add actual composite-action cache-hit tests for stale `latest`, corrupted exact-version bytes, and wrong metadata. Declare the WASM-specific installed-version verification path explicitly instead of applying a native `callisto --version` expectation indiscriminately.

7. High — Production activation ordering and rehearsal identity are not concretely enforceable.

   Orchestration `T006` installs the automatic production trigger and removes its current gate; the replacement exact-candidate activation gate appears only in `T010`, after rehearsal. Prose says to block activation but does not establish a disabled production entry point before T006 or specify how the exact candidate evidence reaches the enabled workflow. This matters because the first production run must not be the test of the new boundary.

   Additionally, `T007` categorically prohibits a `callisto@X.Y.Z` tag while product `PM-004` necessarily derives exactly that tag. The spec prohibits addressing the production tag namespace, so isolation must be expressed as repository plus tag identity, or a specified staging product identity—not an incompatible standalone tag ban.

   Correction: establish the fail-closed activation mechanism before introducing the automatic trigger; exercise disabled production behavior in a negative test. Define the staging repository/product binding concretely and verify that production credentials and repository targets remain unreachable.

8. Medium — Verification commands and file inventories are not executable as written.

   Orchestration `T002/T003` run `cargo nextest ... -p callisto-graph --test durable_release_e2e_tests`, but that target exists under `callisto-cli/tests`, not graph. Several orchestration tasks bypass AGENTS.md’s mandatory `just`/`moon` route. Setup `S-004` says `just ci` includes repository contract tests; the live Justfile’s `ci` dependency list does not include those shell tests.

   Several steps remain “implement the gated contract” without a chosen API or concrete baseline, particularly new remote Git operations and recovery handoffs. That falls short of navigator’s implementation-ready requirement at precisely the changed interfaces.

   Correction: add appropriate task-runner targets, correct crate/test ownership, and wire the new shell suites into persistent CI. State the selected API signatures and integration points rather than requiring implementers to design them during execution.

Per-plan recommendations:

| Plan | Recommendation | Blocking findings |
|---|---|---|
| PRODUCT-MODEL-001 | FAIL | 1–5 |
| CONVERGENCE-002 | FAIL | 1–3 |
| ORCHESTRATION-003 | FAIL | 1, 2, 4, 7, 8 |
| MEMBERSHIP-AUTHORITY-004 | FAIL | 3 |
| SETUP-IMMUTABLE-VERSION-005 | FAIL | 6, 8 |
| Program | FAIL | Unresolved semantic ownership and executable dependency ordering |

No plan explicitly proposes restoring Environment approval, journal authority, or local-tag authority; their stated direction correctly rejects those. The findings above show where implementation gaps or sequencing can preserve the old behavior or prevent the new contracts from becoming executable. No files were edited.
